lines.text: AI can help you learn faster, or help you learn nothing at all. Today you choose the first one.
When you are stuck on a chapter, ask the AI to explain it like you are 10.
Ask for an everyday example from your own life to make it easy to picture.
Then explain it back in your own words to make sure you really get it.
Ask the AI to quiz you one question at a time and wait for your answer.
Testing yourself is one of the best ways to remember things.
Tell the AI not to give you the answer, but to ask you questions instead.
This turns the AI into a coach, so your own brain does the thinking and the learning.
AI sometimes invents facts, dates or names that sound completely real.
Check every important fact against your textbook or a trusted website.
Write what you checked in a fact-check table.
Never hand in AI work as your own.
Ask your teacher what AI use is allowed, and say when you used it.
Use AI to learn, not to skip the learning.
Here the learner asks for a simple explanation with a familiar example and a set length.
The kitchen comparison makes a hard idea easy to picture and remember.
The AI made a quiz, but its answer to question one is wrong.
Our science textbook says photosynthesis happens in the chloroplasts, not the mitochondria.
We write this in our fact-check table and tell the AI to correct it.
In Socratic mode, the AI asks questions instead of giving the answer.
You do the thinking, so you can solve the next problem on your own in the exam.
Your fact-check table has four columns: what AI said, what the source says, right or wrong, and the fix.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
